reviews.verdict: Revise; plausible mechanism, low workload confidence and low integration readiness.
reviews.objection: The nine rubric dimensions are addressed, but the core cache invariant needs a sharper design. Prefix hits require contiguous committed ancestry: declining a suffix block can make later blocks unusable as a prefix. Promotion also requires recomputing a block whose first copy was declined. The cited RR-Evict abstract supports tail eviction, not this admission rule; #51981 supplies a simpler request-level comparator. Neither the 75% cacheability target nor the supplied sources establish avoidable eviction on DEP8 or two DEP4.
reviews.required_revision: Specify ancestry-preserving admission, hash recording and promotion after recomputation, and behavior for hybrid cache groups, asynchronous commits, cancellation, and speculative rollback. Compare stock admission, #51981 no-store, and RR-Evict at equal KV capacity and request order. Use a small block-lifecycle test and CPU replay to check recomputed tokens before a matched serving A/B. Report TTFT tails, scheduler cost, HBM use, throughput, and agent/tool quality separately for each topology; keep deployment and publication novelty unestablished.

reviews.verdict: Major revision; mechanism is distinct, but the commit protocol and value test are underspecified.
reviews.objection: The nine rubric dimensions are present, yet an all-rank acknowledgement alone cannot make an in-place expert-weight migration atomic: moving weights may invalidate the old map before the new map is published. Shadow slots or a quiescent migration boundary may consume HBM or stall serving. #62009 already removes host work from the decode critical path and reports single-node rearrangements; its GB200 decode-only DEP16/DEP32 results do not establish benefit for B200, 8K prefill/1K output, or either proposed layout. #61839's bounded rebalance count is a stronger low-complexity comparator than the card currently emphasizes.
reviews.required_revision: Define whether migration uses shadow storage or a serving pause, how each rank versions and acknowledges weights and maps, and how timeout preserves a valid old placement. Make expiry choose safe defer/discard, never an unsafe forced commit. Compare EPLB off, best fixed placement, existing async cadence, and a rebalance cap with equal expert memory. First use a component test of migration cost, rank skew, and free HBM; then run matched serving at relevant concurrency on DEP8 and two DEP4, measuring TTFT, TPOT, throughput, migration pauses, cost per token, and quality. Resolve the active MoE backend and pinned-baseline inclusion before claiming implementation readiness.

global_gaps: The draft returns two cards against a requested maximum of five; the shortfall is appropriate given the evidence. Each card names three explored directions, but should state the distinct failure mode and cheapest falsifier for each rejected direction.

The pinned vLLM and DeepSeek Serve revisions are historical baselines. The supplied #62541 guide PR is open against main, and #62073 is open on a stacked branch with a reported conflict; neither its merge-commit field nor later main availability proves inclusion in the pinned deployment. #62009 base/head and pinned inclusion remain unknown.
The supplied pinned flashinfer_moe_ep.py body is absent. The later #62073 body and diff cannot establish the active B200 backend, EPLB path, or cache lifecycle at the pinned revision.

No supplied B200 request, block, rank, or kernel evidence establishes cache thrashing, durable expert skew, migration payback, or the winning topology. These are experiment questions; neither proposal warrants a speedup estimate.

Resolve checkpoint, precision, KV format, MTP/DSpark state, and chat/tool quality before comparing policies. The #62417 report concerns the 1017 checkpoint on SM120 and is a qualification warning, not evidence that the specified B200 deployment has the same failure.
